1. Core Clinical Tension: A 69-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with a 3-month history of chronic pelvic pain and an isolated 5-cm mass in the uterine fundus on pelvic ultrasound. In postmenopausal patients, solitary uterine fundal lesions are almost uniformly presumed to be uterine leiomyomas, degenerating fibroids, or stromal neoplasms, making an isolated primary uterine hydatid cyst an unexpected diagnosis.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Triage evaluation ends with initial pelvic clinical examination, baseline pelvic ultrasound demonstrating the 5-cm uterine fundal mass, and plain chest radiography, immediately prior to send-out hydatid ELISA serology, targeted scan interpretation, and surgical cyst resection.
3. Differential Distinctions: Degenerated uterine leiomyoma is the most prevalent etiology for a solitary 5-cm fundal mass in elderly women; uterine sarcoma or endometrial malignancy is considered given new postmenopausal pelvic pain; definitive serology (ELISA titer 1/320) and histopathologic identification of characteristic hydatid cyst layers establish echinococcal disease.
case_prompt:
A 69-year-old overweight woman (BMI 27 kg/m²), menopausal for 16 years and multiparous (G6P4A2) with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, presents with chronic pelvic pain of 3 months duration. She has no prior history of abdominal surgery.

On physical examination, her abdomen is soft and non-tender without palpable masses. Speculum examination demonstrates a macroscopically healthy cervix. Bimanual examination reveals a painless, small uterus without adnexal fullness. The remainder of the clinical examination is unremarkable.

Initial pelvic ultrasonography demonstrates a well-defined 5-cm mass located in the uterine fundus. Plain chest radiography demonstrates clear lung fields without focal parenchymal lesions.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Uterine leiomyoma (cystic or degenerating uterine fibroid)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A 5-cm uterine fundal mass in a 69-year-old woman is typically regarded as a benign fibroid, and the patient underwent surgery under the preoperative presumption of a benign cyst/leiomyoma, but histopathologic evaluation confirmed a parasitic hydatid cyst.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: we opted for a conservative treatment since we operated the patient with a preoperative diagnosis of a benign cyst

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The development of a symptomatic 5-cm pelvic mass in a woman 16 years post-menopause raised concern for neoplastic disease, but complete imaging revealed no invasive features or metastatic deposits, and histopathology confirmed a hydatid cyst.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: An additional scan substantiated the presence of a 5 cm hydatid cyst in the uterine fundus, with no other localizations detected

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) demonstrated strongly positive hydatid serology at a titer of 1/320, and conservative surgical dome resection confirmed a solitary primary hydatid cyst of the uterus.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The hydatid serology was positive (1/320) according to the ELISA technique (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay).

editor_comments: Admission narrative strictly adheres to the admission breakpoint before serology and pathology. Direct quotes verified.
